subject: Service impact: streaming chunk failures & intermittent 500s (eu regions)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ops - SentinelMed <ops@sentinelmed.com>, Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@sentinelmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Service impact: streaming chunk failures & intermittent 500s (eu regions)

Hi Aisha / SentinelMed ops team —

Quick note to let you know we're seeing an elevated error rate for streaming responses and a small number of 500s for the /v1/generate endpoints originating from eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. We're actively triaging — initial signal (09:03 UTC) shows a spike in partial-chunk failures where streams terminate early and some full-request 500 responses. Your account traffic shows ~2.6% of requests affected in the last 30 minutes.

What we've done so far (short):
- Deployed a routing rule to preferentially route your requests to eu-west-2 as a temporary fallback.
- Increased retry threshold at the edge (3 -> 5) for streaming chunks to absorb transient flaps.
- Pulled a diagnostic snapshot and attached a trimmed log dump for your review (incident-dump-logs-20280719.txt).

Immediate ask: please confirm whether you see client-side errors (stream truncation) on your end and whether you'd like us to route all traffic to eu-west-2 for the next 2 hours.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RWI-2028-07-19-eu-streaming (we've posted a brief incident banner).

I'll follow up with a timeline and root-cause once we complete the first-pass triage. Thanks for your patience — we're treating this as high priority.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-dump-logs-20280719.txt (plain text, trimmed), impact-timeline-20280719.csv
From: Ops - SentinelMed <ops@sentinelmed.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Service impact: streaming chunk failures & intermittent 500s (eu regions)

On 19 Jul 2028 09:12, Dylan Brooks wrote:
> Quick note to let you know we're seeing an elevated error rate for streaming responses...

Thanks Dylan — Aisha and I see intermittent stream truncation on our side (webhooks start, then connection closes after ~3-6s). We rely on partial responses for our patient triage flow so this is causing queued items to backlog.

Please route our production traffic entirely to eu-west-2 for now. Also confirm whether there's any risk of data exposure in these failures — our security team asked for a quick yes/no.

If you can share an ETA for a fix or a short bridge timeline, that would help us coordinate on-call rotations.

— Ops (SentinelMed)
Aisha Kumar
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
ops@sentinelmed.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ops - SentinelMed <ops@sentinelmed.com>, Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@sentinelmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Service impact: streaming chunk failures & intermittent 500s (eu regions) — mitigation & next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks for the quick confirmation and sorry for the disruption. Short update and next steps: 

Summary of findings so far (first-pass):
- Root cause (investigating): a surge of small KV cache evictions in our prefix cache combined with transient network latency to our redis cluster in eu-west-1. The eviction storm caused increased cold-path backend calls and occasional downstream timeouts, which surface as stream truncations and rare 500s.
- Security: NO evidence of data leakage or unauthorized access in the events we've examined. Failures are request-level timeouts and early terminations only. We'll escalate to security if anything changes.

Actions taken (completed):
- All SentinelMed production traffic routed to eu-west-2 (completed 09:35 UTC) — we will keep this in place while we validate.
- Temporary increase in prefix-cache size and adjusted eviction policy to reduce churn (applied 10:20 UTC).
- Tightened circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid cascading backend retries.
- Hotfix queued to change redis connection timeouts and add improved backoff on cache misses; planned deploy at 13:00 UTC behind canary.

Next steps and timeline:
- 13:00 UTC: canary rollout of redis-backoff hotfix (expected 15–30m verification).
- 14:00 UTC: brief sync with your SRE (15 minutes) to confirm behavior and coordinate rollback if necessary. I'll send a calendar invite.
- By 18:00 UTC today: preliminary post-incident note with timeline + corrective actions. Full RCA/doc will follow after deeper log correlation and perf traces.

Attachments: impact-timeline-20280719.csv (per-account request counts and error breakdown).

If you want us to keep traffic routed for longer, say the word — otherwise we'll start rerouting back gradually after the canary shows stable metrics.

Again, apologies for the interruption — we know this impacts your patient flow and we're on it.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
